items.followUp: Define a coordinate covalent bond and explain its formation in the hydronium ion, H₃O⁺.

rubric.why: Defines the distinctive feature of a coordinate covalent bond.
rubric.description: Defines the bond as a shared pair of electrons donated by one atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one atom provides both electrons in the shared pair.

rubric.why: Explains one valid example of coordinate bond formation.
rubric.description: Explains that nitrogen in NH₃ donates a lone pair to H⁺ to form NH₄⁺.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying NH₃ and H⁺, and 1 mark for the donated pair or formation of NH₄⁺.

rubric.why: Explains a second valid example of coordinate bond formation.
rubric.description: Explains that oxygen in H₂O donates a lone pair to H⁺ to form H₃O⁺.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying H₂O and H⁺, and 1 mark for the donated pair or formation of H₃O⁺.

modelAnswer: A coordinate covalent bond is a covalent bond in which both electrons of the shared pair are donated by one atom.
In NH₃, nitrogen donates a lone pair to H⁺, forming NH₄⁺; the N→H bond is coordinate covalent.
In H₂O, oxygen donates a lone pair to H⁺, forming H₃O⁺; the O→H bond is coordinate covalent.

items.followUp: Define solubility and state two factors that affect the solubility of gases in liquids.

rubric.why: Checks the definition, including the specified conditions.
rubric.description: Defines solubility as the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a specified temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the maximum amount/quantity, solute, solvent and temperature.

rubric.why: Tests the general principle relating the nature of solute and solvent.
rubric.description: Like dissolves like: substances with similar polarity tend to dissolve in one another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the principle or correctly matching polar and nonpolar substances.

rubric.why: Tests the temperature principle for solid solutes.
rubric.description: The solubility of most solids in liquids increases as temperature increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct trend for solids.

rubric.why: Tests a general principle for gases in liquids.
rubric.description: Gas solubility decreases as temperature increases; it increases as pressure increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct gas-solubility trend.

modelAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a specified temperature.
Like dissolves like: polar substances dissolve in polar solvents, and nonpolar substances dissolve in nonpolar solvents.
The solubility of most solids in liquids increases with an increase in temperature.
The solubility of gases in liquids decreases with an increase in temperature and increases with an increase in pressure.

items.followUp: What is meant by mass number?

rubric.why: Checks the defining quantity that identifies an element.
rubric.description: Atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for correctly identifying the number of protons in the nucleus; award 1 mark for stating only that it is the number of protons.

modelAnswer: Atomic number is the number of protons present in the nucleus of an atom.

items.followUp: State two differences between an atom and a cation.

rubric.why: Checks the charge distinction between an atom and an ion.
rubric.description: An atom is electrically neutral, whereas an ion carries a charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this correct contrast.

rubric.why: Checks the electron-count distinction or how an ion forms.
rubric.description: A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons; an ion forms when an atom gains or loses electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct contrast.

modelAnswer: An atom is electrically neutral, whereas an ion has a positive or negative charge.
An atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons; an ion has gained or lost electrons, so these numbers are unequal.

items.followUp: State two properties of a proton.

rubric.description: A neutron has no electrical charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is neutral or has zero charge.

rubric.why: Checks another characteristic property of a neutron.
rubric.description: A neutron has a mass of approximately 1 amu and is found in the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either its approximate mass or its location in the nucleus.

modelAnswer: A neutron has no electrical charge.
A neutron has a mass of approximately 1 amu and is present in the nucleus of an atom.

items.followUp: What is carbon dating, and what kind of sample can it be used to date?

rubric.why: Checks the use of the radioactive isotope carbon-14.
rubric.description: Carbon-14 is used to determine the age of fossils or other ancient once-living materials by carbon dating.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the age-determination use and 1 mark for identifying fossils or another suitable ancient sample.

modelAnswer: Carbon-14 is used in carbon dating to determine the age of fossils and other ancient materials that were once living.

items.followUp: What are groups in the periodic table? Name the elements in the second period.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of periods in the periodic table.
rubric.description: Periods are the horizontal rows of the periodic table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying periods as horizontal rows.

rubric.why: Checks the elements in the first period.
rubric.description: The first period contains hydrogen and helium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both elements.

modelAnswer: Periods are the horizontal rows of elements in the periodic table.
The first period contains hydrogen (H) and helium (He).

items.followUp: Define atomic radius and give the atomic radius of hydrogen as an example.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of atomic radius.
rubric.description: Atomic radius is the distance from the nucleus to the outermost electron shell of an atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Checks that an example is given.
rubric.description: For example, the atomic radius of sodium is about 186 pm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant element with an example value, or a clearly identified valid example.

modelAnswer: Atomic radius is the distance from the nucleus of an atom to its outermost electron shell.
For example, the atomic radius of sodium is approximately 186 pm.
